newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's Jan-Nov '96 oil exports rise to $797 mln.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's Jan-Nov '96 oil exports rise to $797 mln.

text.p: The total value of Yemen's crude oil exports in the first 11 months of this year rose to $797.2 million compared with $777.5 million in all of 1995, an official at Yemen's oil and mineral resources ministry said on Monday.
The value of Yemen's crude oil exports in the full year 1990 reached $515.3 million, he said.

The source said the government's share in total oil production "reached 26.69 million barrels for domestic consumption and 39.67 million barrels for export in the same period, compared with 24.23 million barrels for local consumption and 45.89 million barrels for export in 1995".
He said Yemen's share in 1990 stood at 13.09 million barrels for domestic consumption and 23.30 million barrels for export.

Yemen's total oil production rose from mid-October to approximately 365,000 barrels per day (bpd) after its Jannah oilfield came on stream producing 15,000 bpd. Jannah's output is due to rise to 30,000 bpd at the beginning of 1997.
Yemen, a small independent oil producer, is one of the poorest countries in the Arab world.
